sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Transcontinental Container Block Train Expedited Freight Forwarding

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaty between the French Republic and the People's Republic of China (signed 30 May 1984)
France-China Double Taxation Convention with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (1984, as amended by subsequent protocols)
Convention concerning International Carriage by Rail (COTIF, as amended at Vilnius 1999) and its Uniform Rules CIM - applicable to France-China intermodal rail freight

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-49-3; Article L.561-2-2 and Articles R.561-55 to R.561-58 (registration of beneficial owners with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés); Loi n° 2016-1691 du 1er décembre 2016 (Loi Sapin II); Directive (UE) 2015/849 and Directive (UE) 2018/843, as transposed by Décret n° 2018-284 du 18 avril 2018.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of identification document (passport or national identity card) for each shareholder and for the proposed gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National competent authority in the country of issuance (e.g., public security bureau or foreign affairs office in the People's Republic of China)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate / police clearance certificate for each natural person shareholder holding 25% or more and for the proposed gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police authority of the country of residence; for France, the casier judiciaire national (Service de la législation pénale)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and corporate registry extract of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of commerce in the jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., SAMR / provincial administration for market regulation in China)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds attestation and recent bank statement demonstrating the contribution to share capital is clean
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution and/or tax authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (pouvoir) appointing the French incorporation agent, together with a notarized draft declaration in accordance with Article L.223-1 of the Commercial Code
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the jurisdiction where the grantor signs

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory prior to signing the articles of association. Screen all proposed shareholders holding 25% or more, all ultimate beneficial owners, and the proposed gérant against: (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and 833/2014); (ii) the French national asset-freezing register maintained by the Direction générale du Trésor (Fonds gelés); (iii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) the OFAC SDN list as best practice for USD payment rails; and (v) the FATF/GAFI PEP guidance as implemented by Article L.561-10 CMF. Positive PEP or sanction hits trigger enhanced due diligence, independent verification, and senior-management approval. All screening outputs are retained for at least five years and remain available to Tracfin on request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises - INPI (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with name availability verification through the RCS/Infogreffe database (https://www.infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal denomination (dénomination sociale) must be composed of Latin characters; non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese ideograms, Cyrillic or Arabic) must be transliterated into a Latin-alphabet phonetic form for registration with the RCS and the SIRENE database. A secondary trade name may be maintained in the original foreign script, but the statutory legal name must be unambiguous and include the reference to the legal form 'SARL' where applicable.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Établissement de crédit - reserved for licensed credit institutions under Articles L.511-1 et seq. CMF; prior ACPR authorisation required.
Assurance / Mutuelle / Réassurance - reserved for regulated entities under the Code des assurances and Code de la mutualité; prior ACPR authorisation required.
Chambre de commerce et d'industrie - reserved for official territorial CCI bodies.
Notaire / Avocat / Commissaire de justice - restricted professional titles requiring prior competent authority approval.
Croix-Rouge / Emblèmes de Genève - restricted under international humanitarian law.
Réseau ferré national / SNCF Réseau - restricted rail-infrastructure designations under the Code des transports.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory extension of the 30-day name clearance memo is available. If the name is rejected by the Guichet unique, the applicant must first request written grounds from the INPI within 5 business days. Within 15 days of the formal denial, the incorporator may petition the juge commis à la surveillance du registre du commerce et des sociétés at the relevant tribunal de commerce. The supervisory judge may order registration, order modification of the name, or dismiss the petition. A further appeal is available before the cour d'appel within 15 days of the judge's ruling; where the rejection is grounded in public-order police powers, an administrative-law remedy before the tribunal judiciaire remains available.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 to R.223-36 governing sociétés à responsabilité limitée; Articles L.123-1 to L.123-9 and R.123-1 et seq. governing registration and business formalities; Articles L.561-46 and R.561-55 et seq. governing beneficial-owner filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés maintained by the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of company formation and application for registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, together with the signed articles of association and beneficial-owner declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is required; capital may be EUR 1 or more. For cash contributions, at least 20% of subscribed capital must be paid upon incorporation and the balance must be paid within five years of registration. Funds are deposited with a bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts, which issues the certificate of deposit. The funds become available after registration. Contributions in kind generally require valuation by a commissaire aux apports, subject to statutory exemptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts and records the subscriptions for all shares stated in the articles of association and confirms that the required initial cash contributions have been deposited. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [full French address], effective upon registration. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed Gérant of the Company for an unlimited term, subject to applicable law and the articles. RESOLVED, that the Gérant is authorised to complete all filings with the Guichet unique, obtain the Kbis extract, open and operate the Company’s bank accounts, and execute documents necessary to commence the Company’s business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate identity, purpose, ownership, and management
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company promoters and the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the SARL name, verify name availability, define the registered office, corporate purpose, capital allocation, beneficial owners, and gérant. Obtain written consent from the registered-office provider and identity documents for all shareholders and managers. Ensure the proposed business purpose covers freight forwarding, rail logistics coordination, customs-related services where applicable, and ancillary services without exceeding regulated transport activities.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and registered-office evidence
Gérant identification, declaration of non-conviction, and parentage certificate
Description of corporate purpose and business activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent names, addresses, activity codes, signatures, or identity information before submission. Obtain a replacement registered-office certificate where the registry rejects the address evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute articles and deposit share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bank, French notary, or Caisse des Dépôts; Guichet unique for subsequent filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the articles of association and subscription schedule. Deposit at least 20% of each cash contribution into a blocked account in the name of the company being formed. Obtain the certificate of deposit of funds. Document any contribution in kind and obtain a commissaire aux apports report unless a statutory exemption is validly applied.
required_dossiers: Bank, notarial, or Caisse des Dépôts certificate of capital deposit
Contribution-in-kind valuation report or exemption statement, if applicable
Shareholder powers of attorney, if signed by representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank due-diligence queries, correct the subscriber information, and reissue the deposit certificate. If formation is abandoned, follow the depositary’s release procedure for returning funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint the gérant and adopt registered-office resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the appointment decision in the articles or by separate instrument. Record the registered office, powers of the gérant, financial year, share-transfer rules, and authority to complete formation formalities. Execute a concise first-management or first-governance resolution confirming subscriptions, capital deposit, registered office, bank mandate, and regulatory applications.
required_dossiers: Gérant acceptance and declaration of non-conviction
Power of attorney for filing agent, if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace defective signatures or appointment wording and re-execute the instrument. If the gérant is ineligible, appoint a qualifying replacement before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised French legal-announcement journal (journal d’annonces légales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the statutory incorporation notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, gérant identity, and registration details required by applicable rules. Pay the regulated publication charge and retain the publication certificate for the Guichet unique filing.
required_dossiers: Final signed articles or validated corporate particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction or republication if the notice contains a material error. Upload the corrected certificate and retain both versions for the corporate file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the electronic registration and beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI; competent commercial court registry for RCS review
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic company-formation form, select the appropriate activity classification, upload the signed articles, capital certificate, publication certificate, registered-office evidence, identity documents, gérant declarations, and beneficial-owner declaration. Electronically sign, pay applicable registry charges, and retain the filing receipt and tracking number.
required_dossiers: Identity and eligibility documents for the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the INPI and registry portals. Respond within the stated deadline to any deficiency notice, upload replacement documents, correct classification or beneficial-owner data, and resubmit the queried item. Challenge a formal refusal through the competent registry or court procedure where correction is not accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration evidence and activate operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial court registry, INPI, tax administration, URSSAF, and business bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET information after approval. Release deposited capital into the company account, activate accounting and payroll systems, register for VAT where required, and maintain the statutory registers. Before commencing regulated freight-forwarding activity, complete the applicable transport-commissionnaire registration and verify customs, warehouse, dangerous-goods, and terminal requirements.
required_dossiers: Transport and operational authorisations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct post-registration errors through the Guichet unique or registry correction process. Suspend the affected activity until any missing transport, customs, environmental, fire, or occupational approval is obtained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Regional Directorate for the Environment, Planning and Housing (Direction régionale de l’environnement, de l’aménagement et du logement, DREAL), acting under the competent Préfet; the Ministry for Ecological Transition administers the national transport framework.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration in the Register of Transport Commissionnaires (registre des commissionnaires de transport), where the SARL contracts in its own name to arrange or organise the carriage of goods. The registration requires satisfaction of professional capacity, financial standing, and good-repute requirements. A separate operating licence is generally not required for a pure forwarding office that does not operate transport vehicles, terminals, or warehouses.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, through the competent DREAL environmental authority and, where applicable, the regional environmental authority (Mission régionale d’autorité environnementale).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Conditional. A forwarding office is ordinarily exempt from a project-level EIA. Construction or operation of a rail terminal, intermodal yard, warehouse, fuel installation, or other classified facility may require case-by-case examination, full environmental assessment, or an Installation Classée pour la Protection de l’Environnement (ICPE) declaration, registration, or authorisation under the French Environmental Code.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No universal thresholds apply to a forwarding office. Any warehouse, terminal, workshop, fuel installation, or waste facility must comply with its applicable ICPE classification, prefectural order, wastewater discharge permit, air-emission and VOC limits, noise limits, spill-prevention controls, hazardous-material rules, and waste traceability obligations. Waste must be segregated, transferred to authorised operators, and documented through required tracking records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupying or modifying premises, obtain applicable building and planning approvals, fire-safety review, and an opening or compliance opinion for establishments receiving the public where relevant. Maintain emergency exits, fire detection and extinguishing systems, evacuation plans, electrical and lifting-equipment inspections, structural load verification for storage areas, and occupational-risk documentation. Apply the Labour Code requirements for workplace safety, training, accident prevention, and occupational-health monitoring. Separate dangerous-goods, rail-terminal, customs, or warehouse approvals may be required according to the physical operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: French General Directorate of Public Finances (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques – DGFiP); online portal: impots.gouv.fr (professional space); customs authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) for EORI/export clearance; company registration via the Single Business Portal (Guichet Unique) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr and the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File incorporation with the Guichet Unique, which automatically registers the SARL with the RNE, INSEE (allocation of SIREN and SIRET identifiers) and the RCS. The SIREN is the statutory French corporate tax reference. Step 2: File the initial corporate income tax return (n°2065-SD) and obtain the competent local tax office (SIE) for Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) at the registered office's jurisdiction. Step 3: VAT — the SIREN is the base VAT identifier; apply for the French intra-Community VAT number (FR + 2-digit key + SIREN) through the DGFiP upon the first intra-EU transaction (Article 286 CGI). Non-resident suppliers without an EU establishment must appoint a tax representative under Article 289A CGI (Form N°3595-SD). Step 4: INSEE automatically assigns the NAF activity code matching the business purpose, i.e., 52.29B (Affrètement et organisation des transports). Step 5: Obtain an EORI number (FR + SIREN) from DGDDI and subscribe to the DELTA-X electronic export clearance platform. All registrations are completed within 5–15 business days via the Guichet Unique.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Pass_Through_Eligible (Default: SARL is fiscally opaque and subject to corporate income tax (IS) — standard 25%, reduced 15% on the first €42,500 of taxable profit per year for SMEs meeting EU turnover criteria (turnover ≤ €10M). Optional income-tax transparency under Article 239 bis AA CGI for qualifying SARLs whose capital is held by natural persons and with limited corporate investors. Territorial scope under Article 209-I CGI: foreign permanent-establishment profits are taxable in France with a foreign tax credit, or exempt if the territoriality election is made. No tax-exempt zone applies to the registered office).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (a) Election for income-tax transparency under Article 239 bis AA CGI (IR) for eligible closely-held SARLs; (b) Family SARL (SARL de famille) option under Article 239 bis A CGI giving shareholders the treatment of a partnership; (c) Tax group (intégration fiscale) under Articles 223 A et seq. CGI for a French parent holding at least 95% of the subsidiary; (d) Hybrid mismatch re-characterisation under Articles 212 bis and 44 CGI (transposing ATAD Directive 2016/1164 and EU 2017/952) for payments with deduction/non-inclusion imbalances, requiring the SARL to align French relief with the payee's tax treatment; (e) No 'check-the-box' classification exists in French law; foreign tax classifications (e.g., US check-the-box entities) are re-assessed through the DGT under general anti-abuse rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for an established French SARL — VAT liability arises from the first taxable supply (Article 256 CGI). For B2B freight-forwarding and intermodal rail services taxable in France, no turnover threshold applies: the supply is taxed at the place of establishment of the customer (Article 259-1° CGI, Article 44 VAT Directive); a non-established supplier must register or the French customer applies the reverse-charge mechanism (Article 283-1 CGI). For intra-EU B2C distance sales of goods to French consumers, the Union-wide threshold is €10,000 per calendar year (OSS scheme available), and IOSS applies to consignments ≤ €150 imported from third territories.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing reform (Ordonnance n°2022-1416, as amended by the 2025 Finance Act; transposition of Directive (EU) 2020/285): B2B and B2G electronic invoicing becomes compulsory from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-cap entities and from 1 September 2027 for SMEs, using the free Public Invoicing Portal (PPF) or certified E-invoicing Service Operators (PDP). Structured XML formats: Factur-X, UBL, CII. E-reporting of B2B, B2C and foreign transactions must then be transmitted to DGFiP in near-real time (within 5 days after invoice issuance). No digital stamping or fiscal visa applies; the DGFiP relies on real-time data clearance for rail cargo, requiring the invoice to contain the client VAT number, freight contract references (CIM/SMGS consignment number), and the export customs declaration reference.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) export of goods outside the EU customs territory — including goods carried by block train under a CIM/SMGS rail consignment contract evidenced by the EU exit confirmation — and (ii) services directly linked to those exports, namely rail freight carriage, transhipment, customs brokerage, loading/handling and forwarding services performed for the exporter or on his behalf (Article 262-I-1° and Article 266-1°(b) CGI). The commission de transport (freight-forwarding service) is zero-rated only when the underlying transport operation itself is an EU export and is ancillary to the export; the French-established SARL must prove that title in the goods passed to a non-resident buyer before the transport begins and that the service is for the direct needs of the goods. Intra-EU transit legs of an intermodal export movement are zero-rated proportionally; any inland haulage not forming a single export operation is standard-rated. Rail freight to non-EU destinations (e.g., China via the Eurasian corridor) qualifies only upon authentication of the EU exit declaration in the delta-X export system.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration En Douane via DELTA-X) with ECS/ICS2 rail manifest movement reference and MRN (Movement Reference Number)
CIM/SMGS international consignment note (lettre de voiture CIM/SMGS) or railway waybill evidencing exit from the EU customs territory at the relevant border office
Commercial invoice and export sales contract proving transfer of title to the non-resident buyer
Packing list and cargo manifest (train consist) documenting goods in transit
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank transfer receipt demonstrating that the export proceeds have been received from the non-resident buyer (SWIFT wire or Letter of Credit)
Statutory declaration of the SARL (attestation) confirming the service was directly attributable to the export and that the zero-rating conditions under Article 262 CGI are satisfied
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French customs and tax audits verify export zero-rating against the DELTA-X exit records, the CIM/SMGS rail consignment and the bank credit of proceeds (a 180-day collection window is the administrative benchmark for export proceeds repatriation). Where the 0% rate is incorrectly claimed, the DGFiP re-assesses French VAT (20%) under Article 272-2 CGI and applies the 80% penalty for deliberate bad faith (mauvaise foi — 80% under Article 1729(b) CGI) or 100% for abusive concealment; criminal sanctions of up to €500,000 fine and 7 years' imprisonment (Article 1741 CGI) apply for fraudulent VAT schemes. The clawback is retrospective for 3 years for ordinary assessments and 6 years in cases of undeclared or concealed tax fraud (Article L.169 LPF); the statutory manager is personally liable under Article L.267 LPF, and the forwarding agent may be jointly and severally liable for the exporter's VAT under Article 1694 CGI. Compliance files must therefore be retained for at least six years (Article L.102 B LPF).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains a fully convertible Euro regime. Current account transactions (trade, services) are unrestricted and freely convertible without prior approval. Capital account transactions, including profit remittances, dividends, and equity contributions, are convertible subject only to standard tax clearance and reporting thresholds administered by the Direction Générale du Trésor. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal; repatriation is permitted after corporate tax payment with routine documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds applies in France. Exporters retain full flexibility to retain foreign currency or convert to EUR at their discretion. Statutory obligations are limited to timely customs declarations for statistical reporting and complete disclosure in annual corporate tax returns. Non-declaration may trigger penalties but does not compel conversion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs. French regulations under the e-Money Directive and PSD2 impose strict licensing and local partnership requirements. Direct cross-border EMI operations serving French entities face significant legal and compliance constraints.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for initial corporate onboarding and KYC interviews in most cases. Remote video KYC is permitted for standard clients but frequently requires subsequent in-person verification, particularly for entities with international operations or complex structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extracts from the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), shareholder declarations, and UBO identification forms
Audited financial statements, tax filings, and bank references confirming legitimate capital origins
Comprehensive screening reports and declarations of no adverse findings

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 wires with purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY INJECTION'. Verification protocols include board minutes, shareholder agreements, and tax authority confirmations. French correspondent banks facilitate through global networks with enhanced AML monitoring.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements cleared primarily via SWIFT MT103 for supplier payments. Rail freight settlements may utilize Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) under UCP 600. All transactions require matching invoices, export/import declarations, and compliance with French customs procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing with the Registry of the Commercial Court (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year-end; filing must occur within one month of shareholders' approval of the accounts (approval must be within six months of fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file) results in a civil penalty of up to €3,000 per director and possible injunction; persistent failure can lead to dissolution proceedings and strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 3 of the following year for online filers; or by the 2nd working day following May 1 for paper filers; extensions apply for professionally represented taxpayers (May 15)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the assessed tax amount, increased to 10% if unpaid after formal notice, plus 0.4% monthly late interest; deliberate underpayment may trigger additional penalties leading to enforcement and suspension of business rights

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year, due the first working day after September 15; simultaneously with any annual amendment, and must be updated within 60 days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to €7,500 for non-disclosure or inaccurate declaration per individual; criminal sanction of imprisonment up to one year for misrepresentation; administrative removal risk from RCS register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder meeting record and formal minutes (PV d'assemblée)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book (internal statutory record; no filing to tax authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Meeting to approve annual accounts must be convened within six months of fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve accounts punctually can be sanctioned by financial penalty; shareholders may petition court for forced appointment of an agent to convene the meeting; operating validity of transactions may be disputed

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) for SARL if, at fiscal year-end, the company exceeds two of the following three thresholds: balance sheet total > €4,000,000, net turnover > €8,000,000, average staff > 50. Also mandatory when shareholders representing at least one-tenth of capital collectively request; or when the company controls a subsidiary requiring audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (PCG – Plan Comptable Général) pursuant to Articles L.123-12 et seq. of the Commercial Code; IFRS permitted for consolidated annual statements; for intermodal rail freight forwarding, specific provisions under ANC Regulation 2018-02 apply.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file an annual confirmation of beneficial owners with the RCS by September 15. The declaration identifies all individuals exercising control or holding interests meeting the 25% threshold, directly or indirectly. Shareholding transfers require the annual confirmation to be updated within 60 days of the transaction; failure to update triggers the same penalties as non-declaration. The confirmation is integrated in the statutory registers and subject to inspection by administrative authorities.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: €300–€700 per year depending on location and service level (Paris premium or provincial standard)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: €2,500–€8,000 per year for a mid-sized SARL subject to compulsory audit; waived audit scope for below-threshold companies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.0% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) for fiscal years commencing on or after 1 January 2024
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit per fiscal year for qualifying SMEs (turnover below EUR 10 million, capital held at least 90% by natural persons or qualifying SMEs). Research Tax Credit (CIR) of up to 30% of eligible R&D expenditure (capped at EUR 100 million); Innovation Tax Credit (CII) of 20% of eligible innovation expenditure up to EUR 400,000 for SMEs; Young Innovative Enterprise (JEI) exemption for the first two profitable fiscal years; accelerated depreciation on certain capital assets; no specific freight-forwarding tax holiday applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_rule_detail: Under CGI Art. 209, French tax losses carry forward indefinitely after the prior 5-year statutory limit was abolished in 2015; however, annual utilization is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000. A one-year loss carryback (report en arrière) is available, extended to 3 years for losses generated in fiscal years ending on or after 30 June 2014. The figure '5' is retained by the group's audit model as a conservative statutory-state planning baseline; substantive law provides unlimited carryforward with the above-mentioned annual cap.
corporate_income_tax_regime.group_filing_regime: French law does not permit consolidated group taxation; each SARL files as a standalone taxpayer, although an optional 'intégration fiscale' regime (tax consolidation) is available for 95%-owned French subsidiaries of a French parent, which is inapplicable where the ultimate parent is non-resident unless a French intermediate parent is inserted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (Déclaration de résultats) together with the standardized annual financial statement package (forms 2050 through 2059-G, including balance sheet, income statement, fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, maturity analysis, and related-party schedules). Mandatory electronic filing via the EFI/EDI system on impots.gouv.fr or certified EDI-TDFC commercial software; paper filing is not accepted for businesses subject to corporate income tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return filed once per fiscal year. Corporate income tax is prepaid through quarterly instalments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the final balancing payment made at the annual return deadline.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the annual return is due by the second business day after 1 May of the following year. For a fiscal year ending on any other date, the return is due within 3 months of the fiscal year close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN/SIRET number, legal form (SARL), NAF/APE activity code, registered office address, and tax account reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert only the French registered office and French SIREN. Foreign shareholders must not be listed in this box; the SARL remains a French tax resident because its registered office and place of effective management are in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre B - Legal form, capital and management
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form, share capital, number of shares, and particulars of the gérant (managing director).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the gérant is a non-resident, enter his name, country of residence and foreign tax identification number; the management location must remain in France to preserve French tax residency and avoid a foreign permanent establishment characterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover, cost of sales, operating expenses and operating income, including freight forwarding commissions, transit fees, demurrage recoveries and intermodal haulage billings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The full intermediation margin on EURASIA rail block-train services is taxable in France; no territorial or offshore sourcing exception applies to a French-resident SARL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tableau 2053-A, line WQ - Accounting profit before tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit before tax as shown in the statutory financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The profit must reflect arm's length remuneration for the French expediting functions; a sustained loss position combined with profitable foreign affiliates will trigger a transfer-pricing audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reintégrations (non-deductible expenses, penalties, excessive interest, thin-cap disallowed interest) and déductions (participation exemption, tax-exempt income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a non-resident shareholder on bonded loans must respect the French thin-capitalization ceiling (generally a 1.5:1 debt-to-equity ratio) and the arm's length interest rate; excess interest is disallowed and triggers the statutory 25% withholding on mischaracterized distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6060 et seq. - Taxable base at the reduced rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable profit to the 15% reduced-rate band (first EUR 38,120 of profit for qualifying SMEs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL may claim the reduced rate even when wholly owned by non-residents provided the statutory SME conditions (turnover under EUR 10 million and 90% capital held by individuals or qualifying SMEs) are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre Tax credits, lines 600-650 - Tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for CIR, CII, foreign tax credits and withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax credits are claimed by the SARL only; excess credits are refunded or offset against future instalments and are not transferable to foreign shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre Déficits reportables, lines 740-750 - Loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of prior-year losses carried forward into the current taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deficits of the French business are deductible; the annual cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit above EUR 1,000,000 applies; losses cannot be shared with a foreign group parent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic 10% late-payment increase plus 0.20% monthly late-payment interest. If a formal notice is served, the penalty increases to 20% when the return is filed within 30 days and 40% when filed later (CGI Art. 1728). Intentional understatements attract a 40% penalty (mauvaise foi) and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers (CGI Art. 1729). Failure to e-file attracts a EUR 15,000 fine. Persistent non-filing combined with concealment may be prosecuted as tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI, carrying up to EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a French SARL to non-resident shareholders (comprising 12.8% final income tax and 17.2% social levies under the flat-tax regime, CGI Art. 119 bis). Reduction to 0% applies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the beneficiary is an EU/EEA company holding directly at least 10% of the SARL's capital for at least 24 months (or with a sworn commitment to hold that period). Comprehensive DTA rates: 0% for substantive shareholdings under certain treaties (e.g., Germany, Luxembourg), 5% for qualified corporate shareholdings under most OECD-based treaties, and 15% for portfolio investments. A non-EU or non-treaty recipient generally suffers the full 30%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: At-source relief requires delivery to the French paying SARL, before each dividend payment, of (i) a certificate of fiscal residence issued by the foreign tax administration (Formulaire 5000 or the local equivalent), (ii) a Form 5001 self-certification for the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, and (iii) a beneficial-ownership statement and, where applicable, a 24-month holding commitment. The payer must verify the beneficial owner status. If relief was not applied at source, the non-resident shareholder may file a reclaim with the competent French tax office (Direction des impôts des non-résidents) within the later of 31 December of the second year following the withholding or two years from the date of the taxable event. Swift Wire and letter-of-credit remittances must retain the withholding proof and the treaty file for at least 6 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest on bona fide arm's length loans paid to a non-resident lender is exempt from French withholding (CGI Art. 131 quater), provided the lender qualifies as beneficial owner resident in a state that has with France an administrative assistance agreement and is not a non-cooperative jurisdiction (ETNC); interest recharacterized as hidden profit distribution is subject to the 30% dividend withholding. Royalties: statutory withholding of 33.33% applies to license fees for patents, trademarks, know-how, and similar IP paid to non-residents without a French permanent establishment under CGI Art. 182 B; 0% under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive for associated EU/EEA enterprises; treaty rates typically range from 0% to 10% for direct IP ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File apply where the FR_SARL, alone or with related entities (including the foreign parent group), has gross revenue or balance-sheet total assets of at least EUR 400 million, or holds directly or indirectly 50% or more of the capital or voting rights of an entity meeting that threshold, or is itself 50% owned by such a threshold-met entity. The Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Below these thresholds, the tax administration may still demand transfer-pricing documentation within 30 days under Article L.13 B of the French Tax Procedures Code; therefore the SARL should maintain a proportionate documentation file whenever related-party transactions exist with the foreign parent, including intermodal haulage fees, capacity booking commissions, and rebilling of rail charges.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method; Berry ratio is commonly used for freight-forwarding commission income)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a codified economic-substance regime comparable to the UAE ESR, but substance is determinative across three legal fronts: (i) permanent establishment analysis under CGI Art. 209 and DTA Art. 5, (ii) the Principal Purpose Test under Article 7 of the Multilateral Instrument and BEPS Action 6, and (iii) the abuse-of-rights doctrine (abus de droit, L.64 of the Tax Procedures Code). The FR_SARL must demonstrate in France, through premises, employees, board minutes, client contracts, credit-risk management, customs-timeline control, and dispatch decisions, that the Eurasian rail expedition activity is genuinely managed from France; a paper-only contract processor or voyager structure is recharacterized as a shell (société écran) and the taxable margin is re-allocated to the foreign principal, with penalties up to 80%.
